findings.text: docs/evidence/fragments/sn-case-file-generation/scfg-case-file.html:5 emits `name="plan-slug" content="sn-case-file-generation"` with no `<meta` opener or closing `>` (the same line is in case-file.html:5), so the slug is inert text in <head> and any tooling reading the plan-slug meta finds none; the generator emits the bare string at docs/evidence/fragments/sn-case-file-generation/case-file.py:667,671, which is why both fragments carry it.

tests/standard_names/test_review_neighbours.py:329 asserts `out == rows` against the rows the fake graph was handed, and :332 asserts the literal `replace(` appears in the statement, so the test named test_locus_neighbours_rank_by_shared_path_depth_and_normalise_prefix cannot redden if the ORDER BY or the prefix normalisation in SN_LOCUS_NEIGHBOURS is removed; the ranking the new locus channel exists for is unguarded.

imas_codex/standard_names/case_file.py:247 gates the empty-enclosing branch on `len(chain) > 1`, so a source whose single enclosing ancestor reaches the root but states no text gets no missing entry and a complete verdict, contradicting the rule stated in its own docstring at :205 that a source whose enclosing structures carry no text is missing; the evidence population has no row with chain >= 1 and zero statements (all 61 zero-statement rows have chain_depth 0), so the hole is latent rather than measured.

tests/standard_names/test_case_file.py:181 asserts `record.tokens > 1` and :199 asserts `record.provenance["graph_writes"] == 0`, which is the literal the implementation writes at case_file.py:1163; neither can fail for any regression they claim to guard, so the zero-write claim rests on the assembly read-only tests rather than on these lines.
